title: The vertical line test
summary: Slide a vertical line across a graph: if it ever cuts the curve twice, the graph is not a function.
alt: A graph with a movable vertical line. The number of points where the line cuts the curve tells whether it is a function.

hit.label: Cuts
hit.text: Where the line meets the curve.

shapes.text: The line cuts the curve {{cnt|int}} time(s)
More than one output: NOT a function

steps.title: A graph and a vertical line
steps.narration: Every vertical line \( x = c \) stands for **one input**. Where it meets the curve you read the **outputs**. Here the curve is a straight line, \( y = 2x - 1 \).

steps.title: Sweep the line
steps.narration: Slide the vertical line (or press play on **c**). It always meets this curve at exactly **one** point: one input, one output. This is a function.

steps.title: The parabola y = x²
steps.narration: \( y = x^2 \) is also cut **once** by every vertical line, so it is a function.

steps.title: Turn it sideways: x = y²
steps.narration: Now \( x = y^2 \). At \( x = {{c|1}} \) the line meets the curve **twice**: one input gives two outputs. **Not a function.**

steps.title: A circle
steps.narration: A circle is cut twice by most vertical lines, so it is **not** a function either.

steps.title: The vertical line test
steps.narration: If **any** vertical line cuts a graph more than once, the graph is not a function. Choose a curve and test it.

formulas.title: Vertical line test
formulas.tex: \text{function} \iff \text{every vertical line cuts the graph at most once}
formulas.text: More than one cut means one input gives two outputs.

challenges.title: Test the graph
challenges.prompt: A vertical line cuts a graph at two points. Can the graph be a function?
challenges.hint: One input would have two outputs.
challenges.explain: No. The same x would give two different y values.

challenges.title: Count the outputs
challenges.prompt: For \( x = y^2 \) at \( x = 1 \), how many values of y are there?
challenges.explain: \( y = 1 \) and \( y = -1 \): two outputs, so it is not a function.

challenges.title: Which is a function?
challenges.prompt: Which one passes the vertical line test?
challenges.hint: Which one is never cut twice by a vertical line?
challenges.explain: \( y = x^2 \) is a function. The other two are cut twice.

intro: A graph is a function only if no vertical line cuts it twice.
takeaways: One input, one output means one cut per vertical line.
If a vertical line cuts twice, the relation is not a function.

notes.title: Press play
notes.text: Press the play button on c to sweep the line across and watch the number of cuts.
